What is method overriding, and does Python support method overloading?

Supplied answer
Overriding is when a child class defines a method with the same name as the parent's, replacing its
behaviour; super() calls the parent version. Python does not support true method overloading - if you
define two methods with the same name, the last one wins. The same effect is achieved with default
parameters or *args.
